parts.problem_md:
Table 5.1 gives information about aluminium and copper:

**Table 5.1**

|   | Aluminium | Copper |
|---|---|---|
| Density in g/cm³ | 2.7 | 8.9 |
| Melting point / (°C) | 660 | 1084 |
| Electrical conductivity | high | high |
| Other information | Forms a layer of aluminium oxide which preventscorrosion | Some copper compounds are toxic |

Use information from Table 5.1 to answer the following questions.

(i) State why aluminium and copper are used in electrical cables.

[1]

(ii) State why aluminium is used in overhead electrical cables.

[1]

(iii) State why copper is not used to make food containers.

[1]
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> - (i) Both aluminium and copper have high electrical conductivity **[1 mark]**
> - (ii) Aluminium has low density / is lightweight **[1 mark]**
> - (iii) Some copper compounds are toxic **[1 mark]**
> 
> Accept aluminium is preferred because it does not corrode

> **[exam-tip]**
> Use the data given in the table directly — examiners want you to link the property (density, conductivity, toxicity) explicitly to the use, not just restate the use.

parts.problem_md:
Steel is an alloy of iron. There are different types of steel.

Fig. 5.1 shows the arrangement of particles in pure iron and in one type of steel.

![Diagram comparing pure iron’s regular lattice of identical atoms with steel’s lattice, where a few darker, larger atoms disrupt the iron layers](assets/001-diagram-comparing-pure-iron-s-regular-lattice-of.png)

**Fig. 5.1**

(i) Describe what is meant by an alloy.

[1]

(ii) Explain why steel is stronger than pure iron.

[2]

(iii) Stainless steel is an alloy of iron. Stainless steel is used to make cutlery because it is strong.

State one other reason why stainless steel is used to make cutlery.

[1]
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> - (i) A mixture of a metal with one or more other elements **[1 mark]**
> - (ii) Steel contains particles of different sizes **[1 mark]**
> - (ii) Which stop layers of atoms from sliding over each other **[1 mark]**
> - (iii) Stainless steel is hard / resistant to rusting **[1 mark]**
> 
> Accept stainless steel does not corrode

> **[exam-tip]**
> The "different-sized particles disrupt the layers" explanation applies to any alloy being harder than the pure metal — learn this reasoning once and reuse it for any alloy question.
